question: A particle moves along a straight line with displacement $s(t)=2t^4-5t^3+3t^2$ metres. Find its velocity and acceleration at $t=1$ second. Also state the direction of motion at that instant.
explanation: Velocity functionDifferentiating the displacement with respect to time,$$v(t)=\frac{ds}{dt}=8t^3-15t^2+6t$$Velocity at $t=1$$$v(1)=8-15+6=-1\text{ m/s}$$Acceleration functionDifferentiating the velocity,$$a(t)=\frac{dv}{dt}=24t^2-30t+6$$Acceleration at $t=1$$$a(1)=24-30+6=0\text{ m/s}^2$$Direction of motionSince the velocity is negative, the particle is moving in the negative direction of the line at $t=1$ second.Final resultThe velocity is $-1$ m/s, the acceleration is $0$ m/s$^2$, and the particle is moving in the negative direction.

options.A: $v=1$ m/s, $a=0$ m/s$^2$; moving in the positive direction
options.B: $v=-1$ m/s, $a=0$ m/s$^2$; moving in the negative direction
options.C: $v=-1$ m/s, $a=-6$ m/s$^2$; moving in the negative direction
